deliverables.name: algebraic-groups
deliverables.title: Algebraic groups
deliverables.description: Reusable Lean formalization of matrix point groups, finite algebraic group schemes and their coordinate algebras. The library covers unitriangular and upper-triangular groups, diagonal products, split kernels, closed unitriangular stages and their underlying affine-space presentations, finite additive products and positive-stage underlying projections and sections, unitriangular scalar base change and coherence, and selected dimension and geometric results. Coalgebra APIs include field subcoalgebras and finite-dimensional containment, right comodules and finitely generated subcomodule containment, coefficient matrix units, counit ranges and idempotent principal ideal constructors; split free presentations give finite tensor coordinates. Precise hypotheses and exclusions are documented in README.md and the focused mathematical guides. This is not a complete formalization of any cited source.

deliverables.description: Native continuous group cohomology in low degrees; transfer and compact-group degree-one torsion; finite-level Tate deflation, compact exceptional Tate groups and diagrams, compact finite-bar homology and norm-limit sequences. For compact topological groups with discrete jointly continuous coefficients over a topologized ring, every continuous cohomology class lifts from a finite open-normal quotient with invariant coefficients. In positive degrees a class-dependent quotient order annihilates the class. The native open-normal inflation cocone is a filtered colimit in all degrees, including zero, with the actual cohomology topology and arbitrary topological-module targets. Its equality refinements depend on the classes; no fixed-stage injection, uniform bound or closed-boundary-range hypothesis is claimed. For arbitrary finite index types, finite functions are naturally equivalent to coefficient-left tensors over a commutative semiring; for finite groups, the twisted action agrees with the diagonal left-regular tensor action. This algebraic result gives no continuous or topological-representation equivalence. At each fixed acting group, the degree-zero coefficient functor is naturally isomorphic to invariants over a ring with its supplied topology.

deliverables.name: formal-power-series
deliverables.title: Formal Power Series
deliverables.description: Integral weighted negative logarithmic derivatives of native formal-power-series units over arbitrary commutative rings, with group laws, naturality and finite coefficient formulas; and coefficientwise ideal-adically restricted native multivariate power series with finite polynomial reductions, regular-principal internal kernels. Polynomial completion over any commutative coefficient ring is the algebra of series over its adic completion with polynomial images at every original quotient precision; coefficient transport recovers the original restricted-series ring equivalence for adically complete coefficients. Ideal-preserving coefficient maps and arbitrary variable maps on these completed-coefficient series give functorial ring maps with finite source-row fiber sums, including infinite fibers. The polynomial-completion comparison is natural in both directions, with completed-scalar compatibility and raw row-kernel containment, without original completeness or finiteness assumptions. The restricted subring also has a coefficient-ring algebra structure, all-level surjective scalar-linear polynomial reductions, and regular-principal module-quotient equivalences, including a separate native-integer API for default module instances. Over adically complete coefficient rings, every polynomial linear endomorphism extends to the restricted series, with finite-level and kernel-preserving uniqueness laws. Independently of completeness, coefficientwise reduction kernels multiply into the kernel at the sum of their levels, including finite-sum laws. For adically complete coefficient rings, units of the restricted subring are detected by the first polynomial reduction or by constant and nonconstant coefficient criteria, with no finite-variable restriction. Over finitely many variables, restrictedness has a degree-cutoff criterion; if the coefficient ideal is finitely generated, every reduction kernel is the intrinsic algebraic image ideal of its corresponding ideal power. Separate restricted-series modules add coefficient content, intrinsic actual-ring leading terms, division under adic/valuation hypotheses and conditional ideal generation by a finite primitive family. A generic support leaf compares cofinal ideal-adic filtrations on arbitrary modules. Change-of-ideal maps and surjective polynomial reduction work for arbitrary ideals and variables. Local-ring polynomial residue is compatible with valuation-domain residue; injective first-variable regrouping has polynomial and finite-variable reindexing interfaces. Intrinsic leading products and singleton division have separate Hausdorff uniqueness and complete primitive-existence interfaces; first-variable division yields finite-polynomial remainders. A supplied division of X₀^d by a divisor with regrouped residue degree d and nonzero scalar top, with actual remainder support below d, gives constant-unit quotient residue; radical equality and completeness reflect it to a unit. With a nonzero principal-adic parameter in the maximal ideal of a commutative valuation domain, radical equality and completeness, a restricted series whose regrouped residue polynomial has degree d and nonzero scalar top coefficient admits a unique unit multiplier and monic first-variable polynomial of degree d, even among competing multipliers not assumed units; coefficient primitivity is derived from the top term.

Based van Kampen for two-open covers with a common basepoint and path-connected opens and intersection, as a unique-homomorphism universal property and a pushout of groups. A path-connected based open core and charts with that common pairwise overlap give a colimit of their inclusion star when the core and charts cover the space. The raw group colimit is multiplicatively equivalent to the ambient fundamental group, preserving every leg in both directions with independent space and index universes. Inclusion-directed covers by neighborhoods of a supplied basepoint give colimits without path connectedness or intersection closure, with a universal property for arbitrary target monoids in independent universes. Monotone neighborhood covers indexed by directed preorders give the same universal property with compatibility only along index inequalities, and colimit data for the canonical preorder diagram. Signed-period additive-circle and complex-circle fundamental groups have integer coordinates, with signed-loop, inverse, endpoint, nonidentity and homeomorphism-compatibility laws, using Mathlib's quotient coverings. Continuous maps act functorially on path components, with equal actions for homotopic maps, in independent space universes without separation assumptions. Based postcomposition on generalized loops and homotopy quotients for every cube-index type, with positive homomorphisms, based-homotopy invariance and fundamental-group compatibility. Homotopy quotients commute with arbitrary dependent products for all cube indices in independent universes, by coordinate evaluation and loop assembly; for nonempty cube indices with decidable equality this is a multiplicative equivalence for the existing group structures. Raw cubical homotopy quotients canonically identify with path components of the same compact-open generalized-loop spaces, naturally in based postcomposition and compatibly with the empty-index comparison. For singleton index types, the generalized-loop space is homeomorphic to the compact-open based path space through Mathlib's singleton-coordinate equivalence, with full forward and inverse evaluation, constant/reflexive-path laws and based-postcomposition naturality. Index and space universes are independent, without separation or local compactness assumptions on the target. The based homotopy-fiber point projection has class image equal to the preimage of the constant class for every cube index, with range–kernel form for the existing positive groups. Equivalences of cube-index types induce quotient equivalences by reindexing representatives, with inverse, identity, composition and based-postcomposition laws in independent universes. For nonempty indices with decidable equality, the same maps are multiplicative for the existing group structures, without requiring corresponding selected axes. The continuous identity from Mathlib's CompHaus-test topology to the original target topology induces a natural equivalence on every cubical homotopy quotient, multiplicative for nonempty indices with decidable equality. Probe, cube-index and target universes are independent. Unchanged functions lift continuously from every universe-parameterized compactly generated source. Ordinary products preserve universe-parameterized compact generation when one factor is locally compact. For such a compactly generated factor P and any topological A, the refinement of P × A is homeomorphic to P times the refinement of A by the identity functions. Supplied relative homotopies from compactly generated sources lift with unchanged joint cylinder functions, endpoints and arbitrary fixed subsets, with counit inverse and naturality laws. Coverings induce canonical quotient-map injections for nonempty cube indices and bijections for nontrivial indices, without decidable equality. For nontrivial indices with decidable equality, the stock homotopy groups are multiplicatively equivalent, with forward postcomposition and inverse represented by a chosen based generalized-loop lift. Coordinate-face cube boundaries are path connected for nontrivial indices, including infinite ones. Finite cube boundaries are closed, including the empty-index case. For every index type, the boundary complement with its subtype topology is homeomorphic to the real product on that type; for finite indices it is locally compact. A Hausdorff space maps continuously to the one-point compactification of any open subspace by retaining that subspace and collapsing its complement to infinity, without a local compactness assumption. Adding a disjoint point gives a surjection, even for the whole space, and a quotient map when the ambient space is compact. For compact Hausdorff ambient spaces, collapse pullback is a homeomorphism between continuous maps based at infinity and ambient maps equal to the chosen point outside the open subspace, with ordinary compact-open/subtype topologies. Its finite-cube specialization identifies generalized loops with based maps from the one-point compactification of the cube-boundary complement, including empty indices and arbitrary topological targets in independent universes. Relative affine interpolation fixes any agreement subset for maps into real modules with continuous addition and scalar multiplication. Generalized loops in such modules are homotopic relative to the cube boundary to their constant loops, and all their homotopy quotients are subsingletons, including empty indices and arbitrary chosen points. Generic covering-map lifting and based equivalences, monodromy, equivariant fiber maps and deck-group centralizers. A covering map is proper exactly when every point fiber is finite, without separation, local compactness or uniform-degree assumptions. Fiber finiteness is locally constant, with clopen locus including empty fibers and excluding infinite ones. On a preconnected base, properness is equivalent to finiteness of the fiber at any given point. For preconnected total space and a supplied total-space point, finiteness of its fiber suffices without base connectedness or surjectivity. With path-connected total space, monodromy identifies the based fiber with left cosets of the induced image, and properness is equivalent to that subgroup having finite index. The canonical comparison from the categorical coproduct of fundamental groupoids to the fundamental groupoid of the topological coproduct is an equivalence, for arbitrary families without connectivity assumptions. Semilocal simple connectivity uses chosen-center loops contracting in the ambient space, with induced-map reflection, local-homeomorphism transport, covering consequences and a locally path-connected neighborhood refinement. Radial deformations of punctured closed and open balls onto spheres are available in arbitrary real normed spaces. Positive real scaling identifies Circle with each positive-radius complex sphere. Scaling and normalization give strict retractions and circle-fixing deformations of punctured balls. Ordered two-factor based wedges are strictly isomorphic to binary wedges, and both nested binary three-factor wedges flatten strictly to the finite wedge. Forward and inverse maps preserve the ordered factor inclusions and common point, for possibly different factors in an arbitrary common universe. In the named cartesian structure on the ordinary opposite based-homotopy category, the unop of the associator followed by left-nested flattening equals right-nested flattening after applying the quotient functor. Positive-radius inner circles classify punctured complex-ball fundamental groups by the integers, with normalization and scaling maps and a nontrivial positive generator. Compatible functions on a disk attachment descend uniquely to any target type, and continuous descent has the same underlying function. Removing the centres of an arbitrary family of attached closed complex unit disks gives a subspace that strongly deformation retracts onto the original space image, for arbitrary unbased circle maps and independent space and disk-index universes, without connectivity or separation assumptions. Commuting squares of source and target homeomorphisms induce homeomorphisms of ordinary compact-open homotopy fibers at corresponding specified points, with point, full-path, inverse, identity, composition and projection laws. Fibers of product maps are homeomorphic to products of ordinary homotopy fibers, preserving both retained source points and full same-time paths, naturally for arbitrary continuous squares in independent universes. A free source factor splits from the fiber of f composed with first projection: the result is HomotopyFiber f b times the free factor, retaining both source coordinates and the entire original path. Whole continuous-map diagrams, inverse and constructor laws and same-time evaluation hold for arbitrary topologies in three independent universes; arbitrary-square naturality with a continuous free-factor map uses six independent universes. For f equal to identity, the full identity-fiber factor remains.

deliverables.title: General linear groups
deliverables.description: Finite general linear groups over possibly noncommutative semirings and rings: Kronecker products of matrix units with reversed identity-factor inverse witnesses, elementary units, ordered commutators, relative normal closures inside elementary groups, finite stabilization, Whitehead block factorization and doubled relative membership and lifting; rectangular block units for independent finite indices with explicit diagonal units; reindexing, nil and quasiregular ideals, congruence subgroups and quotient lifting, nonunital unitization, and matrix trace modulo additive commutators. Scalar unit reflection for Ring-to-Semiring homomorphisms forces quasi-regularity of the canonical two-sided kernel without surjectivity; for surjective maps it is equivalent to this kernel condition. Source and target universes are independent, with no commutativity or local-ring hypothesis. A square-zero kernel of any Ring-to-Semiring homomorphism identifies units mapping to 1 with the additive kernel via u - 1 and 1 + x; the inverse unit has value 1 - x. All mixed kernel products must vanish, with no surjectivity assumption. For left ideals I, J with I^2 contained in J, original-ring principal units map to the additive layer I/(I intersect J); Jacobson containment of I makes the map surjective and identifies its kernel quotient with that layer. Neither two-sidedness nor J contained in I is required. Dual-number GL, SL and scalar-unit reduction kernels, determinant/trace, coefficient maps and the left-conjugation adjoint action use commutative rings. The trace quotient is an additive group, not a quotient ring; its corner inverse requires a chosen matrix index. A Steinberg presentation adds elementary-symbol relations, universal lifts and a finite map onto the elementary subgroup, without opposite-root or central-extension assertions. Over iterated dual numbers, Mathlib's GL units have an ordered commutator equal to the mixed lift of the associative matrix bracket; its outer reduction-kernel element has complete pure-inner readback. For trace-zero inputs, the refinement in Mathlib's SL group uses special-linear factors, identifies the ordered mixed commutator and reads back its pure-inner trace-zero coefficient in the outer SL kernel. Elementary unit-pivot diagonalization, product-one diagonal membership, continuous elementary paths and finite special-linear elementary neighborhoods add algebraic and topological interfaces with their respective unit-minor, path-connectedness and open-scalar-unit hypotheses. Zero-product rectangular blocks over any ring yield a unit 1 + AB whose stabilization is an elementary ordered commutator of block shears. Stable general linear groups form a direct limit over semirings; over rings their stable elementary subgroup is perfect and equals the commutator subgroup, with quotient canonically the abelianization. Over commutative rings the stable determinant and its quotient and abelianization factorizations admit rank-one sections; the elementary subgroup lies in the determinant kernel. Entrywise matrix ideal-power bounds hold over semirings for arbitrary left ideals and independent finite decidable indices, including empty indices. Any exponent annihilating the whole ideal also annihilates a matrix whose entries lie in it.

A generic pointed Finsupp sum-kernel equivalence underlies this basis. Single-term units over nontrivial semirings are exactly the terms whose coefficient and monoid index are both units. Coefficient-unit reflection holds over every semiring, including the trivial one. For an arbitrary subgroup of a group, its left ideal of basis differences consists of exactly the elements with zero coefficient sums on left cosets. Over a nontrivial ring these ideals reflect subgroup membership and inclusion, and two-sidedness is equivalent to subgroup normality. No group or coefficient commutativity or finiteness is needed. The coset map itself is semiring-general. Subgroup finite generation implies finite generation of its left group-ring ideal over any ring; over a nontrivial ring the converse holds. For the whole group this characterizes finite generation of the augmentation kernel. Left-Noetherian group algebras over nontrivial rings have every subgroup finitely generated. Surjective augmentation combines with the generic surjective-homomorphism Noetherianity theorem for coefficient descent over arbitrary semirings and monoids. For a finitely generated commutative monoid, its monoid algebra over any left-Noetherian ring is left-Noetherian, in independent universes and without coefficient commutativity. Augmentation gives the reverse implication; the exponent monoid need not be finite. For any injective homomorphism from a group to a monoid, left-Noetherianity of the monoid algebra descends to the group algebra over every semiring, with three independent universes. Every subgroup algebra is therefore left-Noetherian, without finite index or normality. The generic criterion uses an additive right retraction and ideal extension-contraction; no target cancellation or freeness is assumed. For any semiring and subgroup, right cosets index a basis of the group algebra as a left subgroup-algebra module, with explicit coefficient, reconstruction and scalar compatibility laws. Finite index makes this module finite over any semiring. For ring coefficients, finite-index subgroup algebras and group algebras are left-Noetherian simultaneously. Over every ring, the infinite cyclic group algebra is left-Noetherian iff its coefficient ring is. Group equivalences and finite-index infinite cyclic subgroups transport this criterion, including finite-group products. Every left ideal of an arbitrary semiring extends along monoid-algebra constants to exactly the elements whose coefficients lie in that ideal. Coefficient-change kernels are therefore extended coefficient kernels. Their powers vanish at exactly the same exponents as the coefficient kernel, including degree zero, for arbitrary semiring homomorphisms and monoids. With ring source and semiring target coefficients, surjectivity identifies the quotient with the target monoid algebra; otherwise it is the range subsemiring. Polynomial transport preserves constants, every coefficient, ideal extension and coefficient-change kernels. For a group-to-monoid map, simultaneous coefficient/index change over a ring source has kernel the sum of the subgroup-relation ideal and the extended coefficient kernel. Surjective coefficients give the algebra of the index range; if the index map is also surjective the full target is available. No nontriviality or commutativity is imposed, and the target coefficients need only be a semiring. No sufficient-condition converse for arbitrary groups is asserted. Over a nontrivial possibly noncommutative ring with prime p equal to zero, nilpotence of the augmentation kernel implies one common p-power exponent for an arbitrary group, hence IsPGroup p G, without finiteness. Uniform vanishing of mixed ordered products gives the same conclusion. A generic left-ideal power API over any semiring identifies zero powers with vanishing of every ordered product of that length, including degree zero. For finite p-groups over any ring with p=0, including the zero ring, the augmentation kernel has zero Nat.card G-th power. Every ordered mixed product of that length therefore vanishes. Over nontrivial rings, finite-group augmentation nilpotence is equivalent to IsPGroup p G. The proof uses central subgroups of order p, canonical cyclic quotient kernels, ideal extension bounds and multiplication of power degrees. For locally finite p-groups over any ring with prime p=0, each augmentation-zero element is nilpotent, with an element-dependent exponent. Under these same hypotheses, the Jacobson radical is the augmentation preimage of the coefficient radical. Radical membership is detected by augmentation, and a basis term is radical exactly when its coefficient is. If the coefficient radical is zero, the group-algebra radical equals the augmentation kernel. No uniform kernel exponent or vanishing kernel power is asserted; noncommutative and zero coefficient rings are allowed. Uniform nilpotence of an ordinary left-ideal action over any semiring yields a nonzero common annihilated vector in every nontrivial semimodule. Two-sided ideals have a canonical common-annihilator submodule, agreeing with commutative set torsion. For any ring and monoid, augmentation-kernel annihilation is equivalent to being fixed by every canonical monoid symbol. Every nontrivial unital module of a finite p-group algebra over a ring with prime p=0 therefore has a nonzero canonical fixed vector, without finite generation, finite dimension or finiteness of the module. Simple modules of these finite p-group algebras have trivial group action on every vector, hence augmentation action. Simplicity over the group algebra is equivalent to simplicity under canonical restriction along singleOneRingHom, including noncommutative and zero coefficient rings. The augmentation-action/trivial-monoid-action characterization is valid for semirings and semimodules. For any map of modules over a finite p-group algebra with prime p=0 in any ring, canonical fixed vectors detect injectivity and canonical augmentation coinvariants detect surjectivity, without finite generation or coupled module universes. The generic injection theorem concerns nilpotent two-sided ideals over semirings acting on additive groups; quotient surjectivity detection allows nilpotent left ideals over rings. deliverables.description: Finite Euler sums for chain and cochain complexes, with native exact-sequence, exact-functor and shift results, plus fixed-arrow relative paths of integer cochain maps in preadditive categories with binary biproducts and pullbacks, and an independent chosen-cokernel quotient-intersection pairing in abelian categories. Also supplies the two exterior snake-sequence maps and proves the four middle exactness positions for an eight-object sequence in abelian categories; the endpoint universal properties and all six interior exactness positions hold without vanishing of the exterior objects. Also gives the canonical Fitting decomposition for endomorphisms of Noetherian and Artinian objects in arbitrary abelian categories, with kernel nilpotence, image invertibility and module-subobject agreement. These decompositions are natural for arbitrary intertwiners on a common tail; the copairing square at each exponent requires only the indicated kernels, images, image map and two biproducts. Separately, either an Artinian or a Noetherian object in a category with zero morphisms and finite biproducts admits a finite indecomposable biproduct decomposition, with an empty family for zero. In an abelian category, an object satisfying both chain conditions admits a finite biproduct decomposition with local canonical endomorphism rings on all factors. Such an object cancels from binary biproducts with arbitrary remaining objects. Finite families with local canonical endomorphism rings and isomorphic biproducts have matching factors, assuming only those two biproducts in a preadditive category. Every endomorphism of a Noetherian and Artinian object in an abelian category has a canonical Drazin inverse, with characteristic equations, unique existence, nilpotent, isomorphism and idempotent comparisons, and an idempotent projector. The kernel and image subobjects of sufficiently high powers equal those of f * drazinInverse f, and f * (1 - f * drazinInverse f) is nilpotent.

deliverables.name: minimal-primes
deliverables.title: Minimal primes
deliverables.description: Classifies minimal primes over nonzero principal ideals in commutative semirings with unique factorization by normalized irreducible factor values. Relates these factors to order-dual irreducible components of principal zero loci. For principal quotients in commutative rings with unique factorization, identifies associated primes with minimal primes over the principal ideal for every generator, and characterizes quotient-spectrum points by associated primes and exact annihilators. For arbitrary dependent families of semifields, classifies all prime ideals of the product by ultrafilters, with zero-set membership, evaluation and germ-kernel bridges, and finite-coordinate and infinite non-coordinate controls. The same equivalence is a homeomorphism for the Zariski and existing Stone topologies, with both basis pullback laws and dense coordinate primes. For arbitrary filters and independently universed dependent semiring fibres, equips the existing total-section Filter.Product with semiring operations, fibrewise maps and principal-filter restriction equivalences. Ultrafilters give division semirings and semifields with pointwise inversion. The section-map kernels are the existing zero-set ideals, compatibly with constant-family germs. Associated primes also transport along compatible algebra maps. In commutative rings with well-founded DvdNotUnit, prime generators give principal ideals of height at most one, with height one for non-zero-divisors and for prime elements in domains. Finite ambient initial height gives well-founded lower intervals in preorders and stabilization of antitone prime chains over commutative semirings, with an ideal interface over commutative rings using only initial FiniteHeight and primeness at every index. Both chain interfaces identify the all-index ideal infimum at the same tail index. For integral homomorphisms of arbitrary commutative rings in independent universes, bounds target Krull dimension by source dimension, with equality for injective maps. Without injectivity, the target has the dimension of the source modulo the kernel. A faithful integral algebra has the dimension of its base ring for its given algebra structure. These results use the full WithBot ℕ∞ dimension, including zero rings and infinite dimension. Minimal primes over arbitrary ideals of finite dependent products of commutative semirings correspond to labelled coordinate minimal primes, using the evaluation-image coordinates of Ideal.piOrderIso. Evaluation comap transports minimality over arbitrary ideals without finiteness of the index. The finite classification includes empty indices, subsingleton factors and whole base ideals, and retains the labels of repeated isomorphic factors.

deliverables.description: Reusable multivariate-polynomial results on infinite-variable ideals, coordinate-difference evaluation ideals, homogeneous evaluation, disjoint-block substitution and its iteration, finite-variable origins of finite collections of polynomial fractions over integral domains in arbitrary fraction-ring representations, and a Krull-dimension bound for subsemirings by their finite-variable fraction-stage preimage dimensions, not the whole stage fields, degree, coefficient extraction and linear evaluation, chosen linear division, existential monic lifts and scalar-top first-variable lex degree. deliverables.name: projective-modules
deliverables.title: Projective modules
deliverables.description: Row-finite linear systems with target satisfying Module.Baer have full solutions whenever every finite set of rows has a solution. Over a semisimple ring this holds for every left module, including modules over division rings; scalars, targets, rows and coordinates have independent universes. Solutions are arbitrary coordinate functions, not necessarily finitely supported functions. Reusable Lean theory of projective modules: finite-projective dual and evaluation base change, invertible modules, exterior algebras and powers, determinants, bounded cancellation and countable absorption, infinite free coordinates, finite stable presentations and IBN-only integer-rank independence, balanced tensor products, right scalar extension and chosen right-free coefficient transport along arbitrary unital semiring homomorphisms, exactness, local and PID freeness, preadditive stable module categories, countably generated submodules over left-Noetherian rings, and locally constant rank and componentwise-free classification. Noncommutative and commutative results retain their distinct hypotheses; rank classification is not asserted for all finite projectives over arbitrary rings. Given an equivalence of module categories over arbitrary rings, finite generation is preserved and reflected with independent scalar and carrier universes. Finite projectivity is preserved with an unrestricted source carrier and target carrier at its scalar/carrier maximum, and is reflected when both carriers are at their corresponding maxima. No linearity, commutativity or freeness premise is imposed on this equivalence interface. Ordinary-coefficient evaluation gives an R-linear equivalence M ≃ₗ[R] ((M →ₗ[R] R) →ₗ[Rᵐᵒᵖ] R) for any semiring R and finitely generated projective left R-module M with additive commutative monoid structure. The first Hom uses the canonical right-regular Rᵐᵒᵖ-action on coefficient R and the second its left-regular R-action. Scalar and source universes are independent; no right action on M, additive inverses or freeness is assumed. Evaluation, inverse and naturality laws accompany the equivalence. Over commutative semirings, two inverse inner-scalar restrictions compare it with Mathlib's Module.evalEquiv, preserving coefficient R and outer scalars R. For commutative semirings and finitely generated projective modules with additive commutative monoid structure, contraction gives a linear endomorphism trace without choosing a basis. Its rank-one evaluation, conjugation and dual-map invariance, cyclicity for maps between two finite projective modules and finite-free comparison with the finite-basis trace retain independent scalar and carrier universes. If the module is an additive commutative group, additivity and cyclicity give trace zero on additive commutators; no ring structure on the scalar semiring is required. For two finite projective additive-commutative-monoid modules, tensoring endomorphisms multiplies their traces, with independent scalar and factor universes. Both bilinear and pointwise forms are provided. Partial trace over a finite projective factor M contracts arbitrary linear maps M tensor N → M tensor P to maps N → P, linearly in the whole input. The untraced factors are arbitrary, with four independent universes. On a tensor product of maps a and b it is trace(a) times b, without normalization. On nonfree projectives the scalar trace need not be a natural multiple of the scalar unit. Product endomorphisms have the sum of their factor traces; diagonal inclusion-projection blocks have the factor traces and off-diagonal blocks have trace zero. An arbitrary block endomorphism of a product of finite projective factors has the sum of its diagonal traces. The off-diagonal formulas assume finite projectivity only of the product, without bases, additive inverses or coupled carrier universes. An arbitrary endomorphism of a finite dependent product of finite projective modules has the finite sum of the traces of its diagonal coordinate composites. The index need only be finite, with independent scalar, index and carrier universes. Over arbitrary rings, the library also describes stably-free kernels of surjections onto finitely generated stably-free targets, finite-coordinate kernel presentations and surjective right-linear matrix kernels. Rectangular right-coordinate maps need finite source coordinates but allow arbitrary target indices; transporting a supplied equivalence needs both indices finite. These constructions use left coefficients and right scalars, without commutativity, injectivity, IBN or equal index cardinalities. Finite projective categories over arbitrary rings are essentially small in the ring universe at independent carrier universes. Ring-universe representatives and linear equivalences give a common reference skeleton for comparing arbitrary input classes. Over a commutative semiring, an idempotent-generated ideal is free exactly for the zero and unit idempotents, without a nontriviality assumption. Right scalar-extension comparisons satisfy pointwise unit and triple-composition associativity laws over arbitrary rings and right modules, with five independent scalar and module universes. A unit semiconjugating two homomorphisms of arbitrary rings induces a fixed-right-target linear equivalence on their scalar extensions, with left multiplication by the unit and its inverse on tensor coefficients. Principal right ideals over arbitrary source and target rings have an image-one scalar-extension equivalence without idempotence, and an image-zero annihilation theorem with idempotence. An idempotent right ideal and its scalar extension are bundled as finite projectives over arbitrary rings, including noncentral matrix idempotents. The right-ideal bundle has an identity linear equivalence to its canonical principal ideal, identifying zero and scalar action. Canonical right regular modules on ordinary semiring carriers are finite and free, including zero semirings. A finite projective common stabilizer can be replaced by a common standard finite free one, without finiteness or projectivity assumptions on the ambient modules. Finite ranks are preserved by ring-universe representatives; finitely generated free categorical objects are classified by finite rank over rings satisfying the strong rank condition, not all finite projectives over arbitrary rings. Finite projective right-module classes form a ring-sized direct-sum monoid and additive Grothendieck group, with arbitrary-carrier generators, universal properties and common finite-projective or finite-free stabilization criteria over arbitrary rings. Over division rings, canonical natural-valued class and integer-valued group dimensions give additive equivalences with ℕ and ℤ, with finite-coordinate and all-integer regular-generator inverses. Scalar extension along arbitrary unital maps between division rings preserves both dimensions and induces bijective class and K₀ maps. For a division-ring source and any ring target, the whole induced maps are independent of the chosen scalar homomorphism. Subsingleton rings give trivial class monoids and groups, not division-ring dimension invariants. Every unital ring homomorphism induces additive scalar-extension maps on right-module classes and K₀, with arbitrary-carrier evaluation and entire-map identity and composition laws over noncommutative and zero rings. The free-word zero-generator augmentation returns the coefficient of the empty word, fixing constants and killing letter monomials. The full-letter linear combination has range equal to its canonical semilinear kernel, under the left regular word-semiring action. These results allow arbitrary, possibly noncommutative or trivial coefficient semirings and empty or infinite alphabets, with independent coefficient and alphabet universes. Over a commutative base ring R and an arbitrary target ring S, right scalar extension agrees with the module-first Mathlib tensor product, with the specified homomorphism-induced coefficient action and right multiplication on coefficients. For commutative S, a separate pointwise comparison lands in the right-module view of Mathlib's scalar-first extension. Pure-tensor, inverse and map-naturality laws retain independent scalar and carrier universes without finiteness or centrality hypotheses.

deliverables.name: valuation-integers
deliverables.title: Valuation Integers
deliverables.description: Power divisibility and a Krull-dimension bound for the integers of a rank-at-most-one valuation, a converse producing rank data from a dimension bound, and intersections of valuation subrings with full residue-field maps. Finite rank-at-most-one intersections have classified primes, dimension at most one and finite spectra whose nonempty opens contain zero. Finite pairwise inequivalent rank-one intersections have a separately hypothesized generic-point fork homeomorphism. Equivalent surjective valuations of a ring into a common cyclic-unit linearly ordered commutative group with zero are equal. A canonical rank-at-most-one valuative topology detects values less than one by convergence of powers; for division rings, the specified identity homeomorphism recognizes equivalence of two rank-at-most-one valuations. Valuations of rank at most one on division rings also have a real absolute-value construction using the specified rank embedding, with comparison lemmas including trivial valuations. Rank-one valuations give nontrivial absolute values, and the associated absolute values are equivalent exactly when the valuations are, even for different ambient value groups. Dense compatible valued-field extensions induce dense integer algebra maps and bijective residue maps, specializing to a reduction-compatible residue equivalence for the uniform completion at arbitrary valuation rank. A dense ring homomorphism preserving raw values exactly identifies the canonical completion of a valued field with a complete separated valued ring over an arbitrary common value group. Dense exactly value-preserving additive maps of valued rings induce uniformities. Bounded submodules of finite-dimensional normed spaces over complete fields are finitely generated over Noetherian coefficient rings whose images contain the norm unit ball, with an extension-integer application. At a positive even index 2k and a prime p with p - 1 dividing 2k, the divided Bernoulli number B_(2k)/(2k) has additive p-adic valuation -1 - v_p(2k) and positive reduced denominator exponent 1 + v_p(2k). For every integer n and positive natural k, the rational expression n^k * (n^k - 1) * (bernoulli k / k) is integral over the integers. More generally, if n^k * (n^k - 1) * q is integral for every natural n, every prime p in the reduced denominator of q satisfies p - 1 divides k. This includes k = 0 and applies to divided Bernoulli numbers at every index. For Henselian valuation integers, a sharp power-root neighborhood has an exact correction value, and the stock power range in the canonical units topology is open when the exponent has nonzero image in the field. For a valuation v on a field with any linearly ordered commutative value group with zero, assume v.valuationSubring is Henselian at its maximal ideal m. For a polynomial f over that subring and a in it, a strict squared-derivative value inequality gives a root b, the exact error/displacement identity, derivative-value equality and uniqueness throughout the original derivative ball. For every natural s, f(a) in m^(2*s+1) and f'(a) not in m^(s+1) give all these conclusions and b-a in m^(s+1), without completeness, rank, discreteness, Noetherianity, monicity or unit-derivative assumptions. For e, d, z in that subring, two algebraic comparisons require no Henselianity: e in m^(2*s+1) and d not in m^(s+1) imply v(e) < v(d)^2, and under the same hypotheses the identity v(e) = v(d) * v(z) implies z in m^(s+1).
